82: fn skip_script_comments<I>(
83:     script_start: TextRange,
84:     comments: &mut std::iter::Peekable<I>,
85:     locator: &Locator,
86: ) -> bool
87: where
88:     I: Iterator<Item = TextRange>,

92:     let index = locator.to_index();

97:         source_len
98:     } else {

100:         match find_newline(opening_tail) {
101:             Some((newline_at, LineEnding::Lf)) => {
102:                 opening_offset + TextSize::try_from(newline_at).unwrap() + TextSize::new(1)
103:             }
104:             Some((newline_at, LineEnding::Cr)) => {
105:                 opening_offset + TextSize::try_from(newline_at).unwrap() + TextSize::new(1)
106:             }
107:             Some((newline_at, LineEnding::CrLf)) => {
108:                 opening_offset + TextSize::try_from(newline_at).unwrap() + TextSize::new(2)
109:             }
110:             None => source_len,
111:         }
112:     };
113: 
114:     if line_end >= source_len {
115:         return false;
116:     }
117: 
118:     let mut row = index.line_index(line_end);
119:     let mut end_offset = None;

122:     while row.to_zero_indexed() < line_count {
123:         let line_start = index.line_start(row, contents);
124:         let line_stop = index.line_end(row, contents);
125:         if line_start >= source_len {
126:             break;
127:         }
128: 
129:         let full_range = TextRange::new(line_start, line_stop.min(source_len));
130:         let full_text = source_code.slice(full_range);
131:         let without_newline = match find_newline(full_text) {
132:             Some((newline_at, LineEnding::Lf)) => &full_text[..newline_at],
133:             Some((newline_at, LineEnding::Cr)) => &full_text[..newline_at],
134:             Some((newline_at, LineEnding::CrLf)) => &full_text[..newline_at],
135:             None => full_text,
136:         };

138:         if without_newline.is_empty() {
139:             break;
140:         }

144:             Some(token) if token.kind() == SimpleTokenKind::Comment => {
145:                 match script_line_content(without_newline) {
146:                     Some(payload) => payload,
147:                     None => break,
148:                 }
149:             }
150:             Some(_) => break,
151:             None => break,
152:         };
153: 
154:         let terminator = content == "///";
155:         if !terminator {

157:             continue;
158:         }
159: 
160:         let next_row = row.saturating_add(1);
161:         if next_row.to_zero_indexed() >= line_count {
162:             end_offset = Some(line_stop);
163:             break;
164:         }
165: 
166:         let next_start = index.line_start(next_row, contents);
167:         if next_start >= source_len {
168:             end_offset = Some(line_stop);
169:             break;
170:         }
171: 
172:         let next_stop = index.line_end(next_row, contents);
173:         let next_range = TextRange::new(next_start, next_stop.min(source_len));
174:         let next_full_text = source_code.slice(next_range);

177:             Some((newline_at, LineEnding::Cr)) => &next_full_text[..newline_at],

179:             None => next_full_text,
180:         };

182:         let next_token = SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(TextSize::default(), next_without_newline).next();
183:         let next_is_embedded_content_line = match next_token {
184:             Some(token) if token.kind() == SimpleTokenKind::Comment => {
185:                 let comment_text = &next_without_newline[token.range];
186:                 let after_hash = comment_text.strip_prefix('#').unwrap_or("");

197:         };

201:             continue;

224: fn script_line_content(line: &str) -> Option<&str> {
225:     let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix('#') else {
226:         // Not a comment
227:         return None;
228:     };
229: 
230:     // An empty line
231:     if rest.is_empty() {
232:         return Some("");
233:     }
234: 
235:     // > If there are characters after the # then the first character MUST be a space.
236:     rest.strip_prefix(' ')
237: }

239: fn is_valid_script_line(line: &str) -> bool {
240:     script_line_content(line).is_some()
241: }

243: /// Returns `true` if line contains an own-line comment.

245:     for char in line.chars() {

248:         }
249:         if !char.is_whitespace() {
250:             return false;
251:         }
252:     }
253:     unreachable!("Comment should contain '#' character")

All 2219 linter tests pass, including the previously failing ERA001 snapshot test.

## Summary

Fixed the ERA001 false positive in `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/eradicate/rules/commented_out_code.rs`:

**Root cause:** In `skip_script_comments` (commented_out_code.rs:82), when a `# ///` terminator is followed by an "embedded content" line (a bare `#` or `# ...` comment, per PEP 723 precedence rules), the scan continues looking for another terminator. If none is ever found, the function returned `false`, meaning the whole script block was treated as invalid and its comments were individually checked — flagging lines like `# dependencies = [` as ERA001.

**Fix** (commented_out_code.rs:120-123, 205-213, 217-219):
1. Record the end of the first terminator that is followed by embedded content (`first_terminator_end`).
